children: What finance options are available for vehicle loans?

A personal unsecured loan may suit borrowers who prefer not to provide an asset as security. A secured car loan uses the vehicle as security with terms up to 84 months. A chattel mortgage allows business buyers to take ownership while the lender holds security. A novated lease allows finance and eligible running costs to be managed through pre-tax salary.
Can I get finance for a used vehicle or private sale?
Yes — we can help finance vehicles bought from private sellers, dealerships, or auctions. We'll also assist with PPSR checks and ownership verification.
What is a low doc loan?

Low doc vehicle loans are available to business owners and self-employed applicants who may not have traditional income documentation. Lending criteria vary between providers and alternative verification methods may be accepted. All applications are subject to lender approval and eligibility requirements.

children: Credit Sense is our expert credit guidance service. We review your credit profile, explain what lenders will see, and help you structure your application for the best outcome.
Will checking my credit score hurt it?
Checking your own credit score (a soft inquiry) does not affect it. Multiple lender applications in a short period can impact your score, which is why we help you apply strategically.
Can you help if I've had credit issues in the past?
Yes — we work with clients across a range of credit profiles. We'll be transparent about your options and find lenders suited to your situation.

/blog/how-to-finance-a-car-queensland.description: Buying a car in Queensland? This step-by-step guide breaks down every finance option available — from secured loans to chattel mortgages — so you can drive away with confidence.

children: How to Finance a Car in Queensland: A Complete 2026 Guide
Buying a car in Queensland? This step-by-step guide breaks down every finance option available — from secured loans to chattel mortgages — so you can drive away with confidence.

attrs.alt: Buying a new car in Queensland — Smartway Finance

children: Buying a car is one of the biggest financial decisions most Australians make. Whether you're after a brand-new vehicle or a quality used car, understanding your finance options before setting foot in a dealership can save you thousands — and a lot of stress.

Before you start browsing listings, get clear on what you can realistically afford. A good rule of thumb is to keep total vehicle costs — loan repayments, insurance, registration, fuel and maintenance — under 15–20% of your monthly take-home income.
Use our free loan calculator to model different scenarios. Getting a clear number upfront puts you in a stronger position at the dealership.
There are several ways to finance a car in Queensland. The right choice depends on whether you're buying for personal or business use, your credit profile, and how much flexibility you want.
The most common option. The vehicle acts as security, typically resulting in lower rates and longer terms — up to 84 months. Works for new and used vehicles from dealers or private sellers.
If you prefer not to use the vehicle as collateral, an unsecured loan gives you full ownership from day one. Rates are generally a little higher to reflect the lender's additional risk.

For vehicles used primarily for business, a chattel mortgage lets you take ownership while the lender holds a security interest. There may be GST and tax deduction advantages — your accountant can advise on your specific situation.

Available through your employer, a novated lease lets you bundle vehicle payments — and sometimes running costs — into your pre-tax salary. This can reduce taxable income, though the structure is more complex.

Your credit score directly influences which lenders will approve you and at what rate. Check your credit report for free through Equifax or Illion before applying. Even small errors can affect your score — dispute anything that looks incorrect.

children: Every formal loan application creates a 'hard enquiry' on your file, which temporarily lowers your score. A broker like Smartway Finance identifies the best-fit lender before applying — protecting your score from unnecessary hits.
Step 4: Compare Lenders — Not Just Rates

The headline interest rate is just one factor. The comparison rate (which includes fees and charges), repayment flexibility, early payout conditions, and the lender's approval speed all matter. Accessing 40+ lenders through a broker means you're comparing the market, not just the two or three options your bank offers.

Pre-approval tells you exactly how much you can borrow before you start shopping. It puts you in a strong negotiating position — the dealer knows you're serious and ready to move. Most pre-approvals are valid for 30–90 days.

Once you've found the right vehicle, your broker finalises the application, handles documentation (including PPSR checks for private sales), and manages settlement from end to end. For most clients, the whole process takes just a few days.

Getting independent finance advice before you sign anything is one of the smartest moves you can make. A broker works for you — not the lender — comparing options across a wide panel to find the right fit for your situation.

That said, if you're a business owner eligible for a chattel mortgage, buying new can unlock stronger tax advantages that change the equation.

children: What is a Chattel Mortgage? A Business Finance Guide for 2026
A chattel mortgage is one of the most popular business vehicle finance structures in Australia — but how does it actually work, and is it right for your business?

attrs.alt: Chattel mortgage business vehicle finance Australia

children: If you're a business owner looking to finance a vehicle or equipment, you've probably come across the term 'chattel mortgage'. It's one of the most commonly used business finance structures in Australia — and for good reason. But the name is a bit misleading, so let's break it down clearly.
How Does a Chattel Mortgage Work?

In a chattel mortgage, 'chattel' simply refers to a moveable asset (like a vehicle or piece of equipment). The business takes ownership of the asset immediately, while the lender takes a mortgage — a legal security interest — over the asset as collateral for the loan.

Unlike a personal car loan where the vehicle may be subject to a security interest of the lender, with a chattel mortgage you're on the title from day one. Once the loan is fully repaid, the lender's security interest is discharged and you own the asset outright.
Who is a Chattel Mortgage Right For?

attrs.class: w-5 h-5 rounded-full bg-[#00B0FF]/15 flex items-center justify-center shrink-0 mt-0.5

attrs.class: w-5 h-5 rounded-full bg-[#00B0FF]/15 flex items-center justify-center shrink-0 mt-0.5

children: Operators looking for flexibility with balloon payments at the end of the term

children: Tax implications of business finance depend on your specific structure, GST registration, and how the asset is used. The information here is general in nature — your accountant can confirm what applies to your situation.

children: Balloon payments must be budgeted for — they're due in full at the end of the term
Chattel Mortgage vs Other Business Finance Options

In a finance lease, the finance company retains ownership throughout the loan term. You pay to use the asset. At the end, you typically have the option to buy, extend, or return it. This can suit businesses that want off-balance-sheet treatment or plan to upgrade regularly.

A commercial hire purchase is similar to a chattel mortgage but structured as a hire agreement — you don't own the asset until the final payment is made. The accounting and tax treatment differs, so your accountant's advice is important here.

For most business owners buying a vehicle or piece of equipment they intend to keep, a chattel mortgage offers the clearest structure and strongest combination of ownership benefits and potential tax advantages.

A Business Finance Guide for 2026","description":"A chattel mortgage is one of the most popular business vehicle finance structures in Australia — but how does it actually work, and is it right for your business?","image":"https://swfin.com.au/images/commerical-finance-loans-australia-02-smartway-finance.jpg","datePublished":"2026-05-28","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Smartway Finance"},"publisher":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Smartway Finance","logo":{"@type":"ImageObject","url":"https://swfin.com.au/smartway-logo.png"}}}Finance HubBusiness Finance 6 min read28 May 2026What is a Chattel Mortgage? A Business Finance Guide for 2026A chattel mortgage is one of the most popular business vehicle finance structures in Australia — but how does it actually work, and is it right for your business?If you're a business owner looking to finance a vehicle or equipment, you've probably come across the term 'chattel mortgage'. It's one of the most commonly used business finance structures in Australia — and for good reason. But the name is a bit misleading, so let's break it down clearly.How Does a Chattel Mortgage Work?In a chattel mortgage, 'chattel' simply refers to a moveable asset (like a vehicle or piece of equipment). The business takes ownership of the asset immediately, while the lender takes a mortgage — a legal security interest — over the asset as collateral for the loan.Unlike a personal car loan where the vehicle may be subject to a security interest of the lender, with a chattel mortgage you're on the title from day one. Once the loan is fully repaid, the lender's security interest is discharged and you own the asset outright.Who is a Chattel Mortgage Right For?Sole traders, companies, partnerships, and trusts registered for GSTBusinesses that use the vehicle primarily (more than 50%) for business purposesBusiness owners who want to claim the GST on the purchase upfrontBusinesses that want to claim depreciation and interest as tax deductionsOperators looking for flexibility with balloon payments at the end of the termKey BenefitsImmediate ownership — the asset appears on your balance sheet from day oneGST on the purchase price may be claimed in full in the next BASInterest payments are generally tax-deductible as a business expenseDepreciation can be claimed on the asset over timeBalloon payments reduce monthly repayments and can be tailored to your cash flowCompetitive rates — often lower than consumer finance productsAlways Speak to Your AccountantTax implications of business finance depend on your specific structure, GST registration, and how the asset is used. The information here is general in nature — your accountant can confirm what applies to your situation.Important ConsiderationsThe asset must be used primarily for business purposesYou're responsible for maintenance and insurance (unlike a lease)Early payout may attract break costs depending on the lenderBalloon payments must be budgeted for — they're due in full at the end of the termChattel Mortgage vs Other Business Finance Optionsvs Finance LeaseIn a finance lease, the finance company retains ownership throughout the loan term. You pay to use the asset. At the end, you typically have the option to buy, extend, or return it. This can suit businesses that want off-balance-sheet treatment or plan to upgrade regularly.vs Commercial Hire PurchaseA commercial hire purchase is similar to a chattel mortgage but structured as a hire agreement — you don't own the asset until the final payment is made. The accounting and tax treatment differs, so your accountant's advice is important here.For most business owners buying a vehicle or piece of equipment they intend to keep, a chattel mortgage offers the clearest structure and strongest combination of ownership benefits and potential tax advantages.SSmartway Finance TeamGold Coast Finance Broker · ACL #566769Free QuoteReady to apply?Get a no-obligation quote from our team. children: 7 Ways to Improve Your Credit Score Before Applying for a Loan
Your credit score is one of the biggest factors in whether you get approved — and at what rate. Here's exactly how to improve yours before you apply.

attrs.alt: Improve your credit score before applying for a loan

children: Your credit score is one of the most significant factors in whether a lender approves your application — and what interest rate they may offer you. The difference between a 'good' and 'excellent' score can potentially mean thousands of dollars over the life of a loan.

Australian lenders use comprehensive credit reporting, which means your file shows both positive and negative information: repayment history, credit enquiries, defaults, court judgements, and the types of credit you hold. A good broker will review your report before submitting any applications.

attrs.class: w-6 h-6 rounded-full bg-[#00B0FF] text-[#01579B] text-xs font-black flex items-center justify-center shrink-0 mt-0.5

children: Consider paying every bill on time — even small utilities and phone bills. Late payments generally stay on your file for 2 years.

attrs.class: w-6 h-6 rounded-full bg-[#00B0FF] text-[#01579B] text-xs font-black flex items-center justify-center shrink-0 mt-0.5

children: Consider reducing your credit card balances. High utilisation (using more than 30% of your limit) may signal risk to lenders.

attrs.class: w-6 h-6 rounded-full bg-[#00B0FF] text-[#01579B] text-xs font-black flex items-center justify-center shrink-0 mt-0.5

children: Try to avoid applying for multiple credit products in a short period. Each application typically triggers a hard enquiry.

attrs.class: w-6 h-6 rounded-full bg-[#00B0FF] text-[#01579B] text-xs font-black flex items-center justify-center shrink-0 mt-0.5

children: Consider keeping old credit accounts open — a longer credit history can often help your score.

attrs.class: w-6 h-6 rounded-full bg-[#00B0FF] text-[#01579B] text-xs font-black flex items-center justify-center shrink-0 mt-0.5

children: Check your credit report for errors. Inaccurate defaults or wrong personal details are more common than you might expect.

attrs.class: w-6 h-6 rounded-full bg-[#00B0FF] text-[#01579B] text-xs font-black flex items-center justify-center shrink-0 mt-0.5

children: Consider paying off any outstanding defaults if possible. Even partial payment may help in some cases.

attrs.class: w-6 h-6 rounded-full bg-[#00B0FF] text-[#01579B] text-xs font-black flex items-center justify-center shrink-0 mt-0.5

children: Give it time — consistent, positive behaviour over 6–12 months can make a measurable difference.
What NOT to Do Before Applying

attrs.class: w-5 h-5 rounded-full bg-[#00B0FF]/15 flex items-center justify-center shrink-0 mt-0.5

children: Apply at multiple lenders simultaneously — this can stack hard enquiries on your file

attrs.class: w-5 h-5 rounded-full bg-[#00B0FF]/15 flex items-center justify-center shrink-0 mt-0.5

children: Take out new credit cards or buy-now-pay-later accounts where possible

attrs.class: w-5 h-5 rounded-full bg-[#00B0FF]/15 flex items-center justify-center shrink-0 mt-0.5

children: Miss repayments on any existing obligation, even if it may seem minor

attrs.class: w-5 h-5 rounded-full bg-[#00B0FF]/15 flex items-center justify-center shrink-0 mt-0.5

children: Change jobs immediately before applying — some lenders may require 6 months in a role

attrs.class: w-5 h-5 rounded-full bg-[#00B0FF]/15 flex items-center justify-center shrink-0 mt-0.5

children: Make large unexplained cash deposits or withdrawals from your bank account

children: Credit Sense — Know Before You Apply

Our Credit Sense service gives you a full picture of your credit profile before any application is submitted. We identify issues, advise on timing, and structure your application to give you the best chance of approval at the best rate.

Improving a credit score generally takes time. Minor improvements from paying down balances may show within 30–60 days. Negative listings like defaults typically stay on your file for 5 years, though their impact may diminish over time with consistent positive behaviour.
If you're not sure where you stand, the best first step is to request a free copy of your credit report through Equifax, Experian, or Illion — you're entitled to one free report per year from each.

children: Accessories and solar setups (in many cases, bundled into the loan)

Both new and used caravans can be financed, including private sales — though the process for private sales involves a few extra steps to verify ownership and ensure there's no encumbrance on the asset.
The most straightforward option. The caravan acts as security for the loan, typically resulting in competitive rates and terms of up to 7 years. You own the caravan outright from day one.
Similar to a secured consumer loan but may offer slightly more flexibility around what's included in the loan. Works well for caravans bundled with accessories.

If you run a business that uses the caravan for income-generating purposes — for example, if you work remotely and travel for work — a chattel mortgage may be appropriate. Speak to your accountant about the eligibility requirements.

Lenders typically finance between $5,000 and $150,000 for leisure assets, depending on the asset value, your credit profile, and your income. Loan terms of 1–7 years are standard, with some lenders offering up to 10 years for higher-value purchases.

A deposit isn't always required — many lenders will finance the full purchase price for qualified applicants. However, a deposit reduces your repayments and demonstrates commitment, which can strengthen your application.
New vs Used Caravans — Does it Affect Finance?

New caravans generally attract lower rates and longer terms. Used caravans — especially older models — may have lender restrictions based on age (commonly, loans must be repaid before the van reaches a certain age). Off-road models may also be assessed differently by some lenders.
